description: Find every cell that starts with a date in a document on this machine: the calendar date, the characters as printed, and the row and column they sit in, numbered as read_table numbers them. The order of day and month is STATED, never guessed: there is no reading of 01/02/2026 that is right everywhere. A row that prints a day and a month without a year is a date only when the year is given, which is how a statement dates its rows. The answer opens with the verdict of the reading, reliable, doubtful or unreadable, and reliable only means nothing looked wrong. The file is read on this machine and never uploaded.

dateOrder.description: Which of the first two numbers is the day. Defaults to DMY, which is how most of the world outside the United States writes a date.

from.description: First row to look in, 1 for the start. Rows keep the numbers read_table gave them.

limit.description: Rows to look in, at most 2000. Defaults to 200. What is left is counted and named, never silently dropped.

maximumPages.description: How many pages to open. Defaults to 40, which bounds a runaway read rather than describing your document: raise it for an annual report.

path.description: Absolute path to the file on this machine. It is read here and never uploaded.

year.description: The year a row without one belongs to, stated once at the top of the document. Left out, such a row is not a date.

name: find_dates

row.description: The row, numbered as read_table numbers it: cite it in check_citations.

written.description: The characters the page printed, untouched.

reason.description: Why the file did not open, when the library could tell: empty, too-big, no-text, too-slow, or the kind of bytes it was. Only on an unreadable verdict.

title: Find the dates a document prints, with the row to cite
